library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Rose_2016b_follitropin_delta")()$meta$reference`
* Description: `r readModelDb("Rose_2016b_follitropin_delta")()$meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40268-016-0126-z>

Rose 2016b characterises the pharmacokinetics of FE 999049 (INN follitropin
delta, a recombinant human FSH expressed in a human cell line) after seven
daily subcutaneous doses of 225 IU. Unlike the companion single-dose analysis
(`Rose_2016_follitropin_delta`, doi:10.1007/s40268-016-0129-9), pituitary
downregulation in this trial was incomplete, so measurable endogenous FSH
was present before dosing. The model therefore describes the measured serum
FSH as the sum of exogenous FE 999049 and endogenous FSH (Eq. 4) in one
central compartment:

* dosing site -> transit compartment -> central compartment (Eqs. 6-7), with
  first-order elimination `k = CL/F / V/F` shared by both FSH sources;
* a zero-order endogenous FSH input `kin` that is suppressed by the observed,
  time-varying inhibin B level through an Imax function with complete
  inhibition possible (Eq. 8);
* an endogenous FSH baseline `FSHbl` that sets the central initial condition
  `FSHbl * V/F` and decreases with baseline progesterone (power function,
  Figure 2);
* `kin` back-calculated per subject from the pre-dose steady state
  (Section 2.2), `kin = k * FSHbl * V/F * (InhB(0) + InhBef) / InhBef`.

# Population

The FE 999049 arm of a randomised, double-blind, active-controlled
multiple-dose trial: 24 healthy women (age 21.5-38.7 years, mean 31.1;
weight 46.1-86.6 kg, mean 71.5; BMI 20.8-28.9 kg/m^2) downregulated with a
1-month GnRH-agonist depot on days -28 and -14 (Section 2.1, Table 1).
Baseline means were FSH 0.211 ug/L (0.089-0.376), progesterone 0.652 ug/L
(0.08-1.49), inhibin B 22.0 pg/mL (4.0-89.0), oestradiol 24.21 pg/mL and LH
0.719 IU/L. Each subject received 225 IU FE 999049 subcutaneously once daily
for 7 days. 672 serum FSH samples were collected (pre-dose, daily for 15
days, and every 4 h from the last dose on day 6 to day 8); 3 were below the
0.075 ug/L LLOQ and excluded.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Rose_2016b_follitropin_delta")()$meta$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F at 65 kg) | 0.423 L/h | Table 2, row CL/F |
| `lvc` (V/F at 65 kg) | 24.3 L | Table 2, row V/F |
| `lktr` (dosing site -> transit) | 0.329 1/h | Table 2, row ktr |
| `lka` (transit -> central) | 0.148 1/h | Table 2, row ka |
| `lrbase` (FSHbl at progesterone 1 ug/L) | 0.162 ug/L | Table 2, row FSHbl; reference 1 ug/L from the Figure 2 curve |
| `e_prog_base_rbase` | -0.246 | Table 2, row Progblef |
| `lec50_inhibinb` | 100 pg/mL | Table 2, row InhBef; Section 3 ('inhibin B concentration giving 50 % inhibition') |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (held constant) | Section 3 and Abstract |
| `etalcl` | 15.6% CV -> 0.024045 | Table 2, IIV CV% column |
| `etalvc` | 18.4% CV -> 0.033296 | Table 2, IIV CV% column |
| `etalktr` | 83.4% CV -> 0.52801 | Table 2, IIV CV% column |
| `etalrbase` | 27.8% CV -> 0.074443 | Table 2, IIV CV% column |
| `addSd`, `propSd` | 0 (not reported) | Section 3: combined additive + proportional model, magnitudes not published |
| `d/dt(depot)` | Eq. 6 | Section 3 |
| `d/dt(transit1)` | Eq. 7 | Section 3 |
| `d/dt(central)` | Eq. 8 | Section 3 |
| `central(0) <- rbase * vc` | FSHbl * V/F | Section 2.2 |
| `kin` back-calculation | pre-dose steady state of Eq. 8 | Section 2.2 |
| Allometric scaling `(WT/65)^e` | reference 65 kg | Section 3; Table 2 footnote |
| `FSHbl * PROG_BASE^Progblef` | un-normalised power function | Section 3; Figure 2 |

IIV variances use `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`, the same conversion the
companion single-dose model applies to the same authors' identically
formatted Table 2.

# Virtual cohort

Covariates are drawn to match Table 1. The paper does not tabulate the
inhibin B time course, so each virtual subject carries an illustrative
daily inhibin B profile shaped after the purple traces of Figure 5: near
baseline for the first days, rising under rFSH stimulation to a peak around
day 7 (peaks of a few hundred to about 6000 pg/mL across subjects), and back
to baseline by day 12. Inhibin B is a measured model input, not a model
prediction, so this profile is a scenario assumption, not a validation
target. As in the paper, the daily value is carried forward between samples.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2016)
n_sub <- 200L

# Relative inhibin B rise above baseline by study day (illustrative shape
# from Figure 5; 0 = baseline, 1 = individual peak).
inhb_shape <- c(0, 0.02, 0.08, 0.2, 0.4, 0.65, 0.9, 1, 0.75, 0.4, 0.15, 0.05, 0, 0, 0, 0)
inhibinb_at <- function(time_h, base, peak) {
  day <- pmin(floor(time_h / 24), length(inhb_shape) - 1)
  base + peak * inhb_shape[day + 1]
}

rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, median, sdlog, lo, hi) {
  x <- stats::rlnorm(n, log(median), sdlog)
  pmin(pmax(x, lo), hi)
}

subjects <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmin(pmax(stats::rnorm(n_sub, 71.5, 9), 46.1), 86.6),
  PROG_BASE = rtrunc_lnorm(n_sub, 0.55, 0.55, 0.08, 1.49),
  INHIBINB_BASE = rtrunc_lnorm(n_sub, 16, 0.75, 4, 89),
  inhb_peak = rtrunc_lnorm(n_sub, 2000, 0.8, 200, 7000)
)

# 225 IU = 13.1 ug, from the specific-activity conversion of the companion
# single-dose paper (Rose 2016, Section 2.2: 37.5/75/150/225/450 IU =
# 2.2/4.4/8.8/13.1/26.3 ug).
dose_ug <- 13.1
dose_times <- seq(0, 144, by = 24)
obs_times <- seq(0, 360, by = 4)

make_events <- function(subj, with_dose = TRUE) {
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subj$id, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  ev <- obs
  if (with_dose) {
    dose <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subj$id, time = dose_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_ug, cmt = "depot")
    ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs)
  }
  ev |>
    dplyr::left_join(subj, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      INHIBINB = inhibinb_at(time, INHIBINB_BASE, inhb_peak),
      treatment = "225 IU (13.1 ug) SC QD x 7"
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-inhb_peak) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events_total <- make_events(subjects, with_dose = TRUE)
events_endo <- make_events(subjects, with_dose = FALSE)

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(events_total[, c("id", "time", "evid")]),
  all(events_total$INHIBINB >= events_total$INHIBINB_BASE)
)
```

# Simulation

The stochastic solve uses the same seed for the total-FSH run (with doses)
and the endogenous-only run (no doses), so each virtual subject keeps the
same random effects in both. Because the model is linear in the central
amount and inhibin B is an external input, total FSH is exactly the sum of
the two components, and the exogenous FE 999049 concentration is the
difference.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Rose_2016b_follitropin_delta")
keep_cols <- c("WT", "PROG_BASE", "INHIBINB", "INHIBINB_BASE", "treatment")

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160430)
sim_total <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_total, keep = keep_cols,
                             covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160430)
sim_endo <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_endo, keep = keep_cols,
                            covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame")

sim <- sim_total |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, treatment, WT, cl, vc, rbase, INHIBINB, Cc) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim_endo |> dplyr::select(id, time, cl_endo = cl, Cc_endo = Cc),
    by = c("id", "time")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc_exo = Cc - Cc_endo)

# Same random effects in both runs: the per-subject clearance must agree.
stopifnot(max(abs(sim$cl - sim$cl_endo) / sim$cl) < 1e-10)
```

A typical-value solve (no IIV; the residual error is zero in this model)
for a 65 kg woman at the cohort-mean progesterone and inhibin B baseline,
with the median-peak inhibin B profile:

```{r simulate-typical}
typ_subj <- tibble::tibble(id = 1L, WT = 65, PROG_BASE = 0.652,
                           INHIBINB_BASE = 22, inhb_peak = 2000)
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ_total <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = make_events(typ_subj, TRUE),
                             covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame")
typ_endo <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = make_events(typ_subj, FALSE),
                            covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame")
typ <- typ_total |>
  dplyr::select(time, Cc, rbase) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc_endo = typ_endo$Cc, Cc_exo = Cc - Cc_endo)
```

# Checks against the paper

## Derived elimination rate and half-life

The paper states that CL/F and V/F for a 65 kg woman give an elimination
rate of 0.017 1/h and a terminal half-life of 40 h (Section 3).

```{r derived}
kel_typ <- 0.423 / 24.3
thalf_typ <- log(2) / kel_typ
c(kel = kel_typ, thalf = thalf_typ)
stopifnot(
  abs(kel_typ - 0.017) / 0.017 < 0.03, # paper rounds to two significant digits
  abs(thalf_typ - 40) / 40 < 0.025
)
```

## Pre-dose steady state

With no dose and inhibin B held at its baseline, the back-calculated `kin`
must hold total FSH exactly at `FSHbl` for the whole trial. Both sides of
this check use the same parameters, so the tolerance is numerical.

```{r steady-state}
ss_events <- make_events(typ_subj |> dplyr::mutate(inhb_peak = 0), FALSE)
ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ss_events, covsInterpolation = "locf",
                      returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12)
fshbl_typ <- 0.162 * 0.652^-0.246
stopifnot(
  abs(ss$rbase[1] - fshbl_typ) / fshbl_typ < 1e-10,
  max(abs(ss$Cc - fshbl_typ) / fshbl_typ) < 1e-6
)
fshbl_typ
```

## Figure 2: endogenous FSH baseline versus progesterone

Replicates the typical-prediction curve of Figure 2. The curve passes
through 0.162 ug/L at progesterone 1.0 ug/L, which identifies the power
function as un-normalised (reference 1 ug/L). The points below are read off
the published curve by the maintainers.

```{r fig2}
fig2_read <- tibble::tibble(PROG = c(0.4, 0.6, 1.0, 1.4),
                            fshbl_fig = c(0.203, 0.183, 0.165, 0.149))
fig2_read <- fig2_read |>
  dplyr::mutate(fshbl_model = 0.162 * PROG^-0.246,
                pct_diff = 100 * (fshbl_model - fshbl_fig) / fshbl_fig)
knitr::kable(fig2_read |>
               dplyr::rename("Progesterone (ug/L)" = PROG,
                             "Figure 2 (ug/L)" = fshbl_fig,
                             "Model (ug/L)" = fshbl_model,
                             "% diff" = pct_diff),
             digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig2_read$pct_diff) < 5))

curve <- tibble::tibble(PROG = seq(0.05, 1.5, by = 0.01)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(FSHbl = 0.162 * PROG^-0.246)
ggplot(curve, aes(PROG, FSHbl)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = fig2_read, aes(PROG, fshbl_fig), shape = 4) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.1, 0.35)) +
  labs(x = "Progesterone (ug/L)", y = "Endogenous FSH baseline (ug/L)",
       caption = "Replicates the typical-prediction curve of Figure 2 of Rose 2016b; crosses are read off the figure.")
```

## Figure 3: visual predictive check of total FSH

Replicates Figure 3. The paper's VPC used 1000 replicates of the 24-subject
trial; here one cohort of `r n_sub` virtual subjects is simulated. The
residual error magnitudes are not published, so the simulated percentiles
carry between-subject variability only and are expected to be narrower than
the observed 2.5th-97.5th percentile band. The observed medians below were digitised from the Figure 3 median line by
the maintainers against the printed axis ticks (about 0.01 ug/L
resolution).

```{r fig3}
fig3_median <- tibble::tribble(
  ~day, ~median_obs,
  0,    0.198,
  1,    0.605,
  2,    0.790,
  3,    1.035,
  4,    1.087,
  5,    1.216,
  6,    1.210,
  6.5,  1.334,
  7,    1.275,
  8,    0.875,
  9,    0.605,
  10,   0.416,
  11,   0.292,
  12,   0.224,
  13,   0.176,
  14,   0.170,
  15,   0.176
)

vpc <- sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = time / 24) |>
  dplyr::group_by(day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p025 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.025),
    p50 = stats::median(Cc),
    p975 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(day)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p025, ymax = p975), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(data = typ, aes(time / 24, Cc), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = fig3_median, aes(day, median_obs), shape = 4, size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (days)", y = "Total FSH concentration (ug/L)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 3 of Rose 2016b. Ribbon: simulated 2.5th-97.5th",
                       "percentiles; solid: simulated median; dashed: typical value;",
                       "crosses: digitised observed median."))

fig3_cmp <- fig3_median |>
  dplyr::left_join(vpc |> dplyr::select(day, p50), by = "day") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (p50 - median_obs) / median_obs)
knitr::kable(fig3_cmp |>
               dplyr::rename("Day" = day, "Observed median (Fig. 3)" = median_obs,
                             "Simulated median" = p50, "% diff" = pct_diff),
             digits = 3)
```

The simulated median reproduces the shape and timing of the observed
median: the rise over the dosing week, the peak 12 h after the last dose,
and the elimination-limited washout. It runs about 5-12 % below the
observed median from day 1 to day 12 and about 15-22 % above it on days
13-15. Both offsets track the illustrative inhibin B input rather than the
PK parameters. Endogenous FSH contributes up to 0.18 ug/L of the total, so
how deeply and how long inhibin B suppresses it moves the total by roughly
0.1 ug/L; the scenario's inhibin B returns to baseline by day 12, so
endogenous FSH recovers faster than it did in the trial, where the
observed day-15 median (0.176 ug/L) was still below the day-0 median
(0.198 ug/L). The typical-value profile for a 65 kg woman reaches
1.313 ug/L at day 6.5 against the observed median peak of 1.334 ug/L.

The checks below use the centre of the comparison and a robust quantile
rather than the worst single day, since the cohort's tails are not
reproducible across rxode2 builds. The bounds leave room for the inhibin B
scenario offsets described above; a mis-transcribed clearance, volume,
dose or unit shifts the whole profile by tens of percent and still fails
them.

```{r fig3-check}
typ_peak <- typ |> dplyr::filter(time > 0) |> dplyr::slice_max(Cc, n = 1)
typ_peak
stopifnot(
  abs(median(fig3_cmp$pct_diff)) < 15,
  stats::quantile(abs(fig3_cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 35,
  # Figure 3 observed median peak, 1.334 ug/L at day 6.5.
  abs(typ_peak$Cc - 1.334) / 1.334 < 0.10,
  typ_peak$time >= 144, typ_peak$time <= 168
)
```

## Figure 5: endogenous FSH suppressed by inhibin B

Replicates the mechanism of Figure 5: the model-predicted endogenous FSH
(solid) falls well below the observed baseline (dashed) as inhibin B
(purple, right axis) rises, and recovers when inhibin B returns to
baseline. Six virtual subjects are shown.

```{r fig5, fig.height = 6}
show_ids <- sort(unique(sim$id))[1:6]
inhb_scale <- 0.4 / 6000
fig5 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(id %in% show_ids) |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = time / 24)
ggplot(fig5, aes(day)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cc_endo), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(data = fig5 |> dplyr::distinct(id, rbase),
             aes(yintercept = rbase), colour = "steelblue", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = INHIBINB * inhb_scale), colour = "purple") +
  scale_y_continuous("Endogenous FSH (ug/L)",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / inhb_scale, name = "Inhibin B (pg/mL)")) +
  facet_wrap(~id) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (days)",
       caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 5 of Rose 2016b with illustrative inhibin B profiles.")

typ_nadir <- min(typ$Cc_endo)
c(baseline = typ$rbase[1], nadir = typ_nadir, day15 = typ$Cc_endo[nrow(typ)])
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic typical-value solve: endogenous FSH never exceeds its
  # baseline after t = 0 because inhibin B never falls below its baseline.
  all(typ$Cc_endo[typ$time > 0] <= typ$rbase[1] * (1 + 1e-6)),
  typ_nadir < 0.25 * typ$rbase[1]
)
```

# PKNCA: exogenous FE 999049 after the last dose

The paper reports no NCA table of its own; its only exposure summary is the
40 h terminal half-life implied by CL/F and V/F. PKNCA is therefore run on
the exogenous FE 999049 component (total minus endogenous) over the last
dosing interval (day 6, 144-168 h) and on the terminal phase from the last
dose to day 15, and the half-life is compared with the paper's value.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc_exo)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, treatment, Cc_exo)
dose_df <- events_total |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 144) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, treatment, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc_exo ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "ug/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "ug")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(144, 144),
  end = c(168, 360),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)

published <- tibble::tibble(treatment = "225 IU (13.1 ug) SC QD x 7", half.life = 40)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published terminal half-life. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

The simulated terminal half-life of the exogenous component agrees with the
paper's 40 h: the dosing-site and transit rate constants (0.329 and
0.148 1/h) are much faster than elimination (0.0174 1/h), so the terminal
phase is elimination-limited. The simulated median is slightly longer,
partly because the paper's 40 h refers to a 65 kg woman while the virtual
cohort averages 71.5 kg and `kel` scales with `WT^-0.25` (about 2 %), and
partly because PKNCA's best-fit terminal window can start while absorption
is still contributing.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error.** The paper used a combined additive and proportional
  residual error model but does not report either magnitude. Both are
  encoded as `fixed(0)`; the companion single-dose model's values (0.038
  ug/L, 0.033) were not carried across because they come from a different
  fit. Simulated observation percentiles therefore reflect between-subject
  variability only.
* **CL/F - V/F covariance.** Reported as positive and significant (Table 3,
  dOFV 11.77) but its magnitude is not printed; the IIV block is diagonal.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as CV% without confidence intervals,
  so it cannot show whether the percentages are exact log-normal CVs or
  `100 * omega`. Variances were computed as `log(CV^2 + 1)`, matching the
  companion single-dose model. Under the `100 * omega` reading they would be
  `(CV/100)^2`; the two differ by under 4 % for CL/F, V/F and FSHbl but by
  32 % for ktr (0.528 versus 0.696).
* **Progesterone reference.** The power function is un-normalised (reference
  1 ug/L), as identified by the Figure 2 curve passing through FSHbl at
  progesterone 1.0 ug/L.
* **kin back-calculation.** The paper states that `kin` is calculated from
  the pre-dose steady state of the other parameters and baseline values but
  prints no formula; setting Eq. 8 to zero at t = 0 with the central amount
  at `FSHbl * V/F` gives the expression in the model, which requires the
  t = 0 inhibin B as the separate time-fixed column `INHIBINB_BASE`.
* **Dose in mass units.** The paper gives only 225 IU; 13.1 ug is the
  specific-activity conversion printed in the companion single-dose paper.
* **Inhibin B time course.** Not tabulated in the paper. The vignette uses
  an illustrative daily profile shaped after Figure 5, carried forward
  between daily values as the paper did (Section 2.1); it is a scenario
  input, not a fitted quantity. Solve with `covsInterpolation = "locf"` to
  reproduce the paper's handling of the daily inhibin B samples.
* **Covariate distributions.** Table 1 gives means and ranges only; weight
  is drawn as normal and progesterone, baseline inhibin B and the inhibin B
  peak as log-normal, truncated to the published ranges.
* **Covariate names.** Baseline progesterone (`PROG_BASE`), time-varying
  inhibin B (`INHIBINB`) and baseline inhibin B (`INHIBINB_BASE`) were added
  to the covariate register for this model, following the time-fixed
  `<X>_BASE` pattern of `CRCL_BASE`.
